rationale.Physical Exam: General Appearance: Full physical exam — broad differential in pregnancy.
rationale.Physical Exam: Abdomen: Obstetric abdominal exam — assess fundal height, tenderness.
rationale.Physical Exam: Neuro / Psych: Headache + visual changes = neurological assessment for end-organ damage.
rationale.Pulse oximetry: Verify oxygenation in pregnant patient with hypertension.
rationale.CBC with differential: Screening. Assess for thrombocytopenia (<100K = severe feature).
rationale.Type and screen / Type and Rh: Baby may need delivery — pre-operative labs essential.
rationale.Urinalysis: Screen for proteinuria — positive in pre-eclampsia. Leads to 24-hour quantitative protein.
rationale.US pelvis (transabdominal, then transvag: Monitor fetus: amniotic fluid volume, EFW. Risk of oligohydramnios and IUGR. TA before TV for placenta previa screening.
rationale.Protein, 24-hour urine, quantitative: ≥300mg in 24h = proteinuria supporting pre-eclampsia diagnosis. May not return before intervention but must be started.
rationale.BMP / CMP / LFTs: Elevated creatinine, LFTs, and uric acid. Screen for HELLP syndrome.
rationale.Betamethasone / Dexamethasone: Antenatal corticosteroids for fetal lung maturity if < 34 weeks. Patient likely to deliver at 33 weeks.
rationale.Magnesium sulfate: Seizure prophylaxis to prevent progression to eclampsia. Standard of care for pre-eclampsia with severe features.
rationale.Labetalol / Hydralazine (IV): IV labetalol is first-line for pre-eclampsia hypertension — superior efficacy with fewer side effects than hydralazine. Nifedipine has fetal effects.
rationale.Consult OB/GYN / Cesarean section: Delivery is definitive treatment. With severe features, deliver ≥ 34 weeks. OB/GYN for cesarean.
rationale.Nifedipine: Can cause reflexive tachycardia and has fetal effects. Not mentioned in ACOG recommendations for pre-eclampsia. Labetalol and hydralazine are preferred.
rationale.Expectant management / discharge home: Pre-eclampsia with severe features is an emergency. Requires ICU/inpatient management. Delivery is definitive treatment.

hpi: {{patient_name}} is a pregnant woman at 33 weeks gestation who presents with facial and upper extremity edema, severe hypertension (189/99), new-onset headaches, and blurry vision — signs of end-organ damage. Pre-eclampsia is defined as SBP > 140 or DBP > 90 developing after 20 weeks gestation WITH end-organ dysfunction (proteinuria, visual/cerebral disturbances, pulmonary edema, creatinine > 1.1, elevated LFTs, or thrombocytopenia < 100,000). With SBP > 160, she meets criteria for pre-eclampsia with severe features. Management triad: (1) Magnesium sulfate for seizure prophylaxis to prevent progression to eclampsia, (2) IV labetalol or hydralazine for blood pressure control (labetalol is superior with fewer side effects), (3) Betamethasone for fetal lung maturity if delivering < 34 weeks. Definitive treatment is delivery — with severe features, deliver at ≥ 34 weeks. OB/GYN consult for cesarean section. Admit to ICU or inpatient unit — this is an emergency.
